title: layer-aware kernel tagging and microburst coalescer for Qwen/Llama (per-layer hints + KV window compression)
author: Evan Kim
description: Motivation: Certain model variants (Qwen medium/large, Llama MQA configs) show episodic microbursts of short-lived attention windows that cause inefficient kernel selection and KV cache churn, increasing p99 latency and token cost. This PR introduces two coordinated runtime mechanisms: 1) layer-aware kernel tagging: a lightweight per-layer hinting API that lets the compiler/runtime prefer narrow-head or wide-head kernels based on historical shape telemetry per-model-version and per-layer; tags are inferred automatically and stored in the model serving metadata with safe fallbacks. 2) microburst coalescer + KV window compressor: a continuous-batching layer that identifies short-duration microbursts (sequences of small token increments < 8 tokens within 50ms) and coalesces them into a microbatch window to amortize kernel launch and KV cache writes. When memory pressure or eviction risk is detected, the KV window compressor opportunistically delta-encodes repeated KV updates (token skyline compression) to reduce peak memory churn and downstream memory copies. Implementation notes: - Non-breaking: default behavior is off for back-compat; enabled via runtime flags (runtime.layer_hints=true, runtime.microburst_coalesce=auto) and via model-profile annotations. - Safe fallbacks: if a tagged kernel path crashes or produces mismatch outputs (detected via unit-level hash checks), runtime falls back to generic kernel and marks the tag as invalid for that model-version. - Telemetry: new metrics (runtime.layer_hint_hits, microburst.coalesce_count, kv.window_compressed_bytes) and a sample trace for coalesced windows. - Model-specific tuning: ship with curated defaults for Qwen-{base,medium,large} and Llama-2-{7b,13b}-MQA derived from synthetic workloads and production traces. Performance: in our internal bench on gec-llama-qwen suite (mixed short/long sequences) we observe p50 token latency improvement of 5-9% and p99 tail reduction of 10-18% for workloads with frequent 1-6 token microbursts; effective token cost drop of ~6% on average due to reduced KV churn and better kernel packing. Backwards compatibility and safety: toggles are gated behind feature flags and sample size thresholds; changes include unit tests and cross-check harnesses against OpenAI/Redwood compat runs. Migration: operators can enable per-deployment via console or config; Dedicated customers get opt-in defaults in next release. This PR is primarily runtime-serving work with small model-profile metadata additions; does not change public API surfaces.

review_conversation: Asha: Could we get more granular gating so we can enable layer hints but not coalescing in Dedicated? Evan: Added separate flags and config keys; documented in runtime/config/flags.rs. Miguel: The fallback path needs to be deterministic to avoid flip-flop in prod under noisy telemetry. Evan: Implemented a sliding window counter and a cooldown period (5 minutes) plus a model-version blacklist for invalid tags. Priya: Need numbers for memory overhead on P4d-16; is KV compression CPU-heavy? Evan: Compression is lightweight delta-encode with 2-3x speed vs memcpy in microbench; memory overhead for compressor buffers is bounded and reclaimed per-window; added microbench numbers to bench file. Miguel: CI flaky on a cross-check test. Evan: Reworked harness to use deterministic RNG seed; CI passed after rerun. Approvals: Asha (approved), Priya (approved), Miguel (approved after minor nit).

See docs/operations/microburst.md for enablement and tuning.
